item.title: [低分少年EX] 台灣國產遊戲機 A'Can 模擬器正式完成！
item.itunes:title: [低分少年EX] 台灣國產遊戲機 A'Can 模擬器正式完成！
item.itunes:author: 低分少年 Low Score Boy
item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kajm0UIzfOw

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解台灣遊戲歷史上極具代表性的本土16位元主機Super A\'Can及其遊戲保存的困境與轉機。
  • 見證開發者如何運用AI技術克服長達二十年無硬體文件的逆向工程難題，大幅提升開發效率。
  • 感受台灣老玩家與開發者跨越二十載的情懷，為保存本土遊戲歷史與文化資產所付出的熱血努力。

摘要

台灣自製主機的遺憾與轉機

由聯華電子旗下敦煌科技於1995年推出的16位元主機Super A\'Can，是台灣遊戲產業史上的一大挑戰，但由於市場失利僅存活約半年，並僅發行過12款遊戲。作者過去曾製作影片介紹這款主機，卻意外使二手市場價格飆漲，導致一般玩家極難親身體驗。如今，在台灣模擬界傳奇人物Billy Jr.的努力下，專屬的A\'Can模擬器終於開發完成，讓這些珍貴的本土遊戲得以重見天日。

AI 助力突破二十年逆向工程瓶頸

早在2000年代初期，開發者便嘗試分析A\'Can，但因缺乏硬體架構文件且晶片皆為客製化設計，開發進度宛如盲人摸象。本次重啟開發借助了OpenAI Codex強大的推論與快速試錯能力，迅速將原本MAME核心僅35%的畫面與15%的音訊完整度推進至90%以上。作者亦親自參與了測試流程，協助逐一排除模擬錯誤與遊戲原生的Bug，使全部12款遊戲皆能在電腦上流暢重現。

技術挑戰與跨越二十載的情懷延續

在攻堅最後10%的完成度時，開發團隊面臨了透明圖層排序及A\'Can高規格16聲道PCM音效（如回音抖動效果）等棘手挑戰，除錯過程消耗了近千美元的AI Token。Billy Jr.早在2002年就曾在巴哈姆特BBS回應作者「這是我們台灣人自己的主機，這個理由就足夠了」，這份初衷驅使他在二十年後與作者攜手完成這款名為Bcan的模擬器。由於原始版權方多已解散，這項成果為台灣本土遊戲文化保存做出了不可磨滅的重大貢獻。

================================================

Developed by UMC subsidiary Funtech Technology,. this 16-bit home video game console was released in 1995. The Super A'Can. was a huge challenge in the history of Taiwan's game industry. Unfortunately, it failed spectacularly. Its lifespan was only about six months,. with just 12 games ever released. I once made a detailed video introducing this console,. so if you'd like to learn more, feel free to check it out. Ironically, I suppose,. because of that video,. prices for A'Can consoles and games on the secondhand market have skyrocketed. I didn't make any money from these sales,. and it actually became much harder for me to complete my A'Can collection. I'm sure it's the same for regular players. There haven't been many opportunities to actually play A'Can games. But now, things have finally changed! Because development of an A'Can emulator. has finally been completed! The A'Can emulator was developed by Billy Jr., a legendary figure in Taiwan's emulation scene. Back in the early 2000s,. he had already tried working with overseas experts to develop an A'Can emulator.

But the A'Can's graphics and sound chips were custom-designed specifically for the console,. and there simply wasn't enough information to analyze them. As a result, development progressed very slowly. Although some initial progress was made,. the overall level of completion remained very low. Now, with the help of AI,. the obstacles that had held development back for years have finally been overcome,. bringing the emulator dramatically closer to completion! I was also very honored. to help with testing during the development process. After all, I guess I'm one of the few people in Taiwan who has spent a lot of time actually playing A'Can games. The testing process did indeed help uncover quite a few emulation bugs. Those bugs were subsequently fixed one by one. At this point, all known issues have been resolved. Seeing A'Can games running smoothly on a computer. is honestly pretty emotional. While most of these games can hardly be called masterpieces,. and quite a few of them can be downright frustrating to play,. at the very least,. from the perspective of preserving the history and culture of Taiwan's domestic game industry,. this is truly a major achievement. Of course, I also asked Billy quite a few questions about the story behind the emulator's development.

First, what prompted him to restart development this time? Billy said it was actually just because his kids were on summer vacation,. so he had more free time. He started working on it in early July and finished it by the end of August,. so it didn't actually take that long. The reason development got stuck in the past. was that he didn't have any hardware documentation. He could only infer the hardware's behavior from the software's output. But that's like trying to figure out an elephant while blindfolded. You can only feel out bits and pieces, and they aren't necessarily correct. Finding the correct answer through trial and error took an enormous amount of time. Fortunately, AI can now help with that. One of AI's strengths is that it has an enormous amount of accumulated knowledge,. and it can run through trial and error very quickly and at low cost. Even if you're trying to figure out an elephant while blindfolded,. AI can take the clues it finds. and tell you, "There's an 80% chance this is an elephant." The MAME emulator already had a basic A'Can core,. but the graphics emulation was only about 35% complete,. and the sound was around 15%. With the help of AI, the level of completion could quickly. be pushed to around 90%!

But trying to go beyond 90%. made that final mile incredibly difficult. You start discovering that many things you thought were correct have to be completely redone. Toward the end, fixing a tiny problem. could end up burning through hundreds of dollars' worth of tokens. For example, layer ordering and transparent color sorting. were among the trickiest parts of development. You can think of it like a pile of cards scattered everywhere. You have to figure out the correct ordering rules. so that when they are stacked back together,. none of the 12 games show any graphical glitches. And to make things even harder, those cards are transparent. So of course, dealing with them was a real pain. During the development of this emulator,. did you discover anything surprising about the A'Can's hardware design? Billy said that, when it comes to sound,. the A'Can features 16-channel PCM audio,. which is actually an insanely high-end specification for the time. But that also makes it very difficult to accurately emulate all of those channels. Take the "echo jitter" sound effect, for example. Billy had originally decided to give up on it. But while fixing the ending music in Speedy Dragon,.

he discovered that the audio channels it used. happened to be perfect for measuring the echo and jitter. That finally allowed him to solve the problem. After all, only 12 A'Can games were ever completed. Some hardware features. might only have been used once, in one specific part of one particular game. You really have to encounter it. before you even realize there's another problem that needs to be solved. And what's even funnier. is that sometimes something initially looked like an emulation error,. only for us to discover later that it was actually a bug in the original game itself. The current version of the emulator. has eliminated all known issues,. but there may still be things we haven't encountered yet. We'll have to wait for players to report them and figure out how to fix them. I was also curious. about which AI tools Billy used, and how much it cost. Billy said he used OpenAI's Codex. with a Pro subscription. He happened to hit several usage resets during development, which saved him quite a bit of money. Since he was also using AI for other projects at the same time,. it's difficult to estimate the exact cost of this emulator.

But he estimates that he still spent around US$700–1,000 on AI. If you ask whether it was worth it,. the answer is definitely yes. After all, he finally fulfilled a dream he'd had for years. and finally put the matter to rest. Back in 2002,. when Billy was discussing on Bahamut BBS. why he wanted to spend time working on an A'Can emulator,. he said, "It's our Taiwanese console. Really, that's reason enough." Those words really moved me back then. And as it happened, Billy's post. was actually a reply to one of my own posts. I never imagined that, more than twenty years later,. I'd actually be able to help Billy. with the development of the A'Can emulator. It's honestly incredible that things came full circle like this. Since the companies that worked on the A'Can console and its games back then. have either gone out of business or left the game industry,. the current status of the relevant rights is unclear. The chances of an official remake or port are pretty slim. While an unofficial emulator isn't exactly the proper way to preserve them,. if it allows these games to be preserved and played,.

surely that's better than letting them be lost forever. Looking back at the A'Can introduction video I made ten years ago,. I personally think the quality in pretty much every aspect. could use a lot of improvement. Now that I can record gameplay footage through the emulator,. with better image quality and much greater convenience,. maybe someday. I'll find the time to make a remastered version of that video. When I was testing it,. the emulator didn't have an official name yet. So I asked Billy if he had any ideas for a name. Billy casually replied, "Bcan?" He was just joking,. but I thought it was an awesome name. "B" comes after "A," and it can also be interpreted as "Backup." But more importantly,. it's "Billy's A'Can emulator." So the official name was confirmed as "Bcan"! For information about Bcan's release and future updates,. please visit the Facebook page. "BillyJr's Emulator World."

It features lots of introductions to classic games and behind-the-scenes stories. I highly recommend giving it a like and following the page! OK, that's it for this Low Score Boy special episode. Thanks for watching, and see you next time!

=============

技術挑戰與跨越二十載的情懷延續

在攻堅最後10%的完成度時，開發團隊面臨了透明圖層排序及A\'Can高規格16聲道PCM音效（如回音抖動效果）等棘手挑戰，除錯過程消耗了近千美元的AI Token。Billy Jr.早在2002年就曾在巴哈姆特BBS回應作者「這是我們台灣人自己的主機，這個理由就足夠了」，這份初衷驅使他在二十年後與作者攜手完成這款名為Bcan的模擬器。由於原始版權方多已解散，這項成果為台灣本土遊戲文化保存做出了不可磨滅的重大貢獻。

================================================

Developed by UMC subsidiary Funtech Technology,. this 16-bit home video game console was released in 1995. The Super A'Can. was a huge challenge in the history of Taiwan's game industry. Unfortunately, it failed spectacularly. Its lifespan was only about six months,. with just 12 games ever released. I once made a detailed video introducing this console,. so if you'd like to learn more, feel free to check it out. Ironically, I suppose,. because of that video,. prices for A'Can consoles and games on the secondhand market have skyrocketed. I didn't make any money from these sales,. and it actually became much harder for me to complete my A'Can collection. I'm sure it's the same for regular players. There haven't been many opportunities to actually play A'Can games. But now, things have finally changed! Because development of an A'Can emulator. has finally been completed! The A'Can emulator was developed by Billy Jr., a legendary figure in Taiwan's emulation scene. Back in the early 2000s,. he had already tried working with overseas experts to develop an A'Can emulator.

But the A'Can's graphics and sound chips were custom-designed specifically for the console,. and there simply wasn't enough information to analyze them. As a result, development progressed very slowly. Although some initial progress was made,. the overall level of completion remained very low. Now, with the help of AI,. the obstacles that had held development back for years have finally been overcome,. bringing the emulator dramatically closer to completion! I was also very honored. to help with testing during the development process. After all, I guess I'm one of the few people in Taiwan who has spent a lot of time actually playing A'Can games. The testing process did indeed help uncover quite a few emulation bugs. Those bugs were subsequently fixed one by one. At this point, all known issues have been resolved. Seeing A'Can games running smoothly on a computer. is honestly pretty emotional. While most of these games can hardly be called masterpieces,. and quite a few of them can be downright frustrating to play,. at the very least,. from the perspective of preserving the history and culture of Taiwan's domestic game industry,. this is truly a major achievement. Of course, I also asked Billy quite a few questions about the story behind the emulator's development.

First, what prompted him to restart development this time? Billy said it was actually just because his kids were on summer vacation,. so he had more free time. He started working on it in early July and finished it by the end of August,. so it didn't actually take that long. The reason development got stuck in the past. was that he didn't have any hardware documentation. He could only infer the hardware's behavior from the software's output. But that's like trying to figure out an elephant while blindfolded. You can only feel out bits and pieces, and they aren't necessarily correct. Finding the correct answer through trial and error took an enormous amount of time. Fortunately, AI can now help with that. One of AI's strengths is that it has an enormous amount of accumulated knowledge,. and it can run through trial and error very quickly and at low cost. Even if you're trying to figure out an elephant while blindfolded,. AI can take the clues it finds. and tell you, "There's an 80% chance this is an elephant." The MAME emulator already had a basic A'Can core,. but the graphics emulation was only about 35% complete,. and the sound was around 15%. With the help of AI, the level of completion could quickly. be pushed to around 90%!

But trying to go beyond 90%. made that final mile incredibly difficult. You start discovering that many things you thought were correct have to be completely redone. Toward the end, fixing a tiny problem. could end up burning through hundreds of dollars' worth of tokens. For example, layer ordering and transparent color sorting. were among the trickiest parts of development. You can think of it like a pile of cards scattered everywhere. You have to figure out the correct ordering rules. so that when they are stacked back together,. none of the 12 games show any graphical glitches. And to make things even harder, those cards are transparent. So of course, dealing with them was a real pain. During the development of this emulator,. did you discover anything surprising about the A'Can's hardware design? Billy said that, when it comes to sound,. the A'Can features 16-channel PCM audio,. which is actually an insanely high-end specification for the time. But that also makes it very difficult to accurately emulate all of those channels. Take the "echo jitter" sound effect, for example. Billy had originally decided to give up on it. But while fixing the ending music in Speedy Dragon,.

he discovered that the audio channels it used. happened to be perfect for measuring the echo and jitter. That finally allowed him to solve the problem. After all, only 12 A'Can games were ever completed. Some hardware features. might only have been used once, in one specific part of one particular game. You really have to encounter it. before you even realize there's another problem that needs to be solved. And what's even funnier. is that sometimes something initially looked like an emulation error,. only for us to discover later that it was actually a bug in the original game itself. The current version of the emulator. has eliminated all known issues,. but there may still be things we haven't encountered yet. We'll have to wait for players to report them and figure out how to fix them. I was also curious. about which AI tools Billy used, and how much it cost. Billy said he used OpenAI's Codex. with a Pro subscription. He happened to hit several usage resets during development, which saved him quite a bit of money. Since he was also using AI for other projects at the same time,. it's difficult to estimate the exact cost of this emulator.

But he estimates that he still spent around US$700–1,000 on AI. If you ask whether it was worth it,. the answer is definitely yes. After all, he finally fulfilled a dream he'd had for years. and finally put the matter to rest. Back in 2002,. when Billy was discussing on Bahamut BBS. why he wanted to spend time working on an A'Can emulator,. he said, "It's our Taiwanese console. Really, that's reason enough." Those words really moved me back then. And as it happened, Billy's post. was actually a reply to one of my own posts. I never imagined that, more than twenty years later,. I'd actually be able to help Billy. with the development of the A'Can emulator. It's honestly incredible that things came full circle like this. Since the companies that worked on the A'Can console and its games back then. have either gone out of business or left the game industry,. the current status of the relevant rights is unclear. The chances of an official remake or port are pretty slim. While an unofficial emulator isn't exactly the proper way to preserve them,. if it allows these games to be preserved and played,.

surely that's better than letting them be lost forever. Looking back at the A'Can introduction video I made ten years ago,. I personally think the quality in pretty much every aspect. could use a lot of improvement. Now that I can record gameplay footage through the emulator,. with better image quality and much greater convenience,. maybe someday. I'll find the time to make a remastered version of that video. When I was testing it,. the emulator didn't have an official name yet. So I asked Billy if he had any ideas for a name. Billy casually replied, "Bcan?" He was just joking,. but I thought it was an awesome name. "B" comes after "A," and it can also be interpreted as "Backup." But more importantly,. it's "Billy's A'Can emulator." So the official name was confirmed as "Bcan"! For information about Bcan's release and future updates,. please visit the Facebook page. "BillyJr's Emulator World."

It features lots of introductions to classic games and behind-the-scenes stories. I highly recommend giving it a like and following the page! OK, that's it for this Low Score Boy special episode. Thanks for watching, and see you next time!

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入瞭解 SEGA 經典格鬥遊戲《VR快打》系列的全新續作《擬真格鬥 命運交鋒》的最新發表資訊。
  • 剖析本作如何融入《人中之龍》與《莎木》風格的動作冒險模式，以及其創新的「命運交鋒」劇情設計。
  • 揭秘本作令人矚目的豪華編劇陣容，包括大衛·海特（David Hayter）與橫山昌義等知名創作者的跨國合作。

摘要

經典格鬥系列的嶄新篇章

SEGA 正式發表了《Virtua Fighter》系列的最新作品《Virtua Fighter Crossroads》（中文官方定名為《擬真格鬥 命運交鋒》）。作者指出，雖然本作並未直接以「六代」命名，但其 Logo 中的「VI」字樣刻意以不同顏色呈現，隱喻了其正統續作的地位。這款新作由研發《人中之龍》系列的「人中之龍工作室」操刀，為這款歷史悠久的 3D 格鬥遊戲注入了全新的生命力。

融入冒險要素與全新主角群

與過去幾乎沒有劇情著墨的舊作不同，本作首次主打著重劇情的單人動作冒險模式。遊戲舞台設定在東南亞的虛構城市「維拉薩帕拉」，這是一座由黑幫掌控、格鬥風氣盛行的混亂都市。故事將圍繞著四位全新主角展開。宣傳片中特別聚焦於其中一位主角「希耶洛」，他因地下格鬥賽的恩怨而招致殺身之禍，並在危急關頭被中華餐館的老闆娘——也就是系列經典角色「陳佩」所救，新舊世代的命運因而產生交會。

豪華的跨國編劇陣容

為了打造引人入勝的單人故事，SEGA 請來了極為奢華的編劇團隊。由知名配音員兼編劇大衛·海特（David Hayter）負責世界觀設定監修，並由資深編劇布萊德·凱恩（Brad Kane）擔任主筆。更令人驚喜的是，人中之龍工作室的橫山昌義與《真·女神轉生》系列的編劇三本真司也加入其中。作者認為，這樣跨越東西方的強大編劇陣容，讓本作的劇情品質非常值得玩家期待。

格鬥系統的繼承與創新

在核心的戰鬥系統上，本作在單人模式中融入了「一對多」的戰鬥機制，透過自動鎖定最近對手與側視角運鏡，在群鬥中依然能維持一對一格鬥的精準度。而在純粹的格鬥模式中，遊戲畫面質感全面提升，招式動作與攻防轉變更像是一部精彩的武打電影。製作團隊也承諾將在簡化操作、降低新手門檻的同時，保留《VR快打》系列傳統的深度心靈博弈，力求讓新老玩家都能享受樂趣。

=============

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-5M7-nhdbZk

SEGA 在 2026 年 6 月 6 日正式發佈了《Virtua Fighter》(VR快打)系列全新作品的第一支正式預告片與內容介紹的特別節目，內容非常精彩，不但有全新主角群，還有舊角色的驚喜現身，遊戲並加入了《人中之龍》甚至該說是《莎木》風格的動作冒險模式，而且編劇群意外大咖！本作當然也保有純粹的格鬥遊戲模式，這則影片簡單統整了這次所發表的資訊。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解「人中之龍工作室」如何透過橫跨五十年的史詩跨度，建構出《Stranger Than Heaven》這款跨時代巨作。
  • 探索本作前所未有的全球豪華卡司陣容，包括史奴比狗狗、多嘉卡潔等國際巨星如何參與其中。
  • 搶先掌握結合「東城會」起源、創新左右手獨立戰鬥系統及聲音模仿玩法等核心遊戲特色。

摘要

跨越時代的命運與混血主角的冒險

作者介紹了由 SEGA 旗下「人中之龍工作室」開發的新作《Stranger Than Heaven》（異於天堂）。故事主角為美日混血的大東真，他為了逃離歧視，搭上前往日本的船隻，並在那裡遇見了影響他一生的人——傳奇走私者奧非斯。大東真在地下社會中，與另一位同樣具有混血背景、心思縝密的青年真誠優發展出一段亦敵亦友的複雜關係，兩人截然不同的個性與目標將成為本作劇情的最大亮點。

星光熠熠的國際化豪華卡司

作者強調本作的卡司陣容極其強大，不僅由成田優與藤岡靛擔綱雙主角，還邀集了包括史奴比狗狗（Snoop Dogg）、多嘉卡潔（Doja Cat）、西岡德馬及太平總名夫等國際級影星參與。最特別的是，製作團隊獲得家屬授權，運用影像技術讓已故傳奇演員松田優作在遊戲中重現，並由宇梶剛士配音。此外，遊戲採用的單一配音版本將體現多國語言交織的寫實感，讓角色展現出自然的文化背景。

五大時代舞台與東城會的起源秘辛

遊戲劇情橫跨了從 1915 年到 1965 年的五個關鍵時代，舞台從福岡小倉、廣島吳市、大阪南區，一路延伸到靜岡熱海與東京新宿。作者透露，本作與《人中之龍》系列有著深刻的淵源，將揭開關鍵組織「東城會」是如何成立的歷史。雖然遊戲內容對新玩家相當友善，但大東真與真誠優兩人名字所隱含的「東城」線索，無疑會讓系列作粉絲感到驚喜與震撼。

創新的獨立肢體戰鬥與聲音錄製玩法

在戰鬥系統上，本作引入了創新的左右手獨立控制，玩家需透過手把的 LR 鍵分別控制主角的手腳，進行直覺的組合攻擊、蓄力或反擊。此外，主角大東真具備獨特的歌唱與聲音模仿天賦，玩家可以在遊戲中錄製環境聲響並協助音樂家編曲。大東甚至能從街頭藝人晉升為表演經紀人，經營並打造專屬的藝人陣容，這項機制類似於系列作中受歡迎的經營支線。

充滿時代氛圍的娛樂活動與發行資訊

作者提到遊戲中收錄了多樣具備時代特色的小遊戲，例如花牌、面子（類似尪仔標）、賽子博弈與獎品射擊等，並包含與女性角色的深度互動。這款內容紮實、充滿娛樂性的作品，預定於 2026 年底至 2027 年初在 Xbox Series、PS5 與 Steam 平台上架，並於發售首日同步登陸 Xbox Game Pass，是一部令人期待的跨時代史詩作。

=============

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EI3V7lhcz3A

SEGA 旗下「人中之龍工作室」的全新作品《STRANGER THAN HEAVEN》是《人中之龍》系列作嗎？有什麼獨特之處呢？SEGA 在 2026/5/7 的直播發表節目中，揭曉了這款作品的眾多特點，因為節目內容很精彩、資訊量又很大，所以我盡快做了個簡單的摘要影片，希望能讓大家快速的認識這款遊戲！
